result.rationale: The migration inserts legacy site_setting values verbatim via `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` with no escaping and no normalization, bypassing the model's before_validation that strips scheme/path. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host then matches via `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, so a legacy entry saved as 'http://eviltrout.com' never matches, breaking embedded comments post-upgrade; a single quote in a value also aborts the migration. The mechanism is fully visible in the diff.

judged_text: The migration's raw INSERT copies legacy embeddable_hosts entries verbatim, applying neither the model's scheme/path normalization (which Fabricate-based specs prove runs on every normal save) nor any SQL escaping. A legacy entry like 'http://eviltrout.com' — which the old SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? explicitly matched by stripping the scheme — is stored as-is and can never satisfy record_for_host's lower(host) = uri.host comparison, so those sites' embedded comments start failing with 'invalid referer host' after the upgrade until an admin manually re-saves each host; additionally a legacy value containing a single quote aborts the migration with a SQL syntax error.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration copies legacy SiteSetting values via a raw SQL string: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. This bypasses `EmbeddableHost` model callbacks (the `before_validation` in app/models/embeddable_host.rb that strips `http(s)://` and paths), so legacy entries like `http://eviltrout.com` will be stored with the scheme and will not match `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` (i.e., `eviltrout.com`). That can cause `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (used by EmbedController/TopicRetriever) to reject previously-allowed hosts after upgrade. Also, interpolating `h` unescaped into SQL means a legacy value containing a single quote will produce invalid SQL and can abort the migration.
